title: Cases Where a Land Use Right Certificate (So Do) Is Not Issued
desc: Which land and buildings cannot get a land use right certificate (so do) under Article 151 of the Land Law 2024: leased land, disputed land, temporary houses.
summary: A summary of the land, houses and works that cannot be issued a Certificate (so do) under Article 151 of the Land Law 2024, with points to check before buying land or building a house.
body: p

Before paying a deposit on land or investing in a house, owners should know whether the plot or the house falls into the cases where a Certificate of land use rights and ownership of property attached to land (commonly called the red book, sổ đỏ) cannot be issued. These cases are listed in Article 151 of Land Law No. 31/2024/QH15.
h2
1. Land for which no certificate is issued
p
Under Clause 1, Article 151, a land user is not issued a Certificate in the following cases:
ul
Agricultural land used for the commune's public-interest purposes (Article 179).
Land assigned for management under Article 7, except for the area assigned or leased for use together with the land assigned for management.
Land leased or sub-leased from another land user, except where leased or sub-leased from an infrastructure-business investor in line with an approved project.
Land received under contract allocation, except where land use rights are recognised under Point a, Clause 2, Article 181.
Land subject to a reclamation decision, except where more than 3 years have passed since the decision without implementation.
Land in dispute, under distraint, or subject to judgment-enforcement security measures or interim emergency measures.
Organisations assigned land free of charge for non-commercial public purposes.
h2
2. Houses and works for which ownership is not certified
p
Under Clause 2, Article 151, property attached to land is not recorded in the Certificate when:
ul
It stands on a plot falling under the cases in Section 1 or on a plot that does not meet the conditions for a Certificate.
It is a temporary house or work: built temporarily while the main work is under construction, or built from thatch, bamboo, reeds, leaves or earth; or an ancillary structure outside the main work.
A clearance notice or decision, or a land reclamation decision, has been issued, except where more than 3 years have passed without implementation.

It was built after the construction ban was announced; it encroaches on protection boundary markers of technical infrastructure works or ranked heritage sites; or it was created after the zoning plan was approved and is not in conformity with the plan at the time of certification – except where a temporary construction permit has been issued.
State-owned property (except State capital contributed to enterprises).
Property that is not among the cases eligible for certification under Article 148 (houses) and Article 149 (construction works other than houses).
h2
3. Situations homeowners often face
ul

Land in dispute with a neighbour: the dispute must be resolved before a certificate can be issued. It is advisable to seek mediation early at the ward or commune People's Committee where the land is located (Article 235).
Level-4 houses with leaf roofs, earthen walls, or temporary sheds: these are not recorded in the certificate; to be certified they must be rebuilt in accordance with regulations.

Building in an area already zoned for roads or parks: a house built after the plan was approved that does not conform to it will not be certified, unless a temporary construction permit has been issued.
Land in an area subject to a reclamation decision: no certificate is issued until more than 3 years have passed without the State carrying out the reclamation.
h2
4. What to check before buying land or building a house
ol
Inspect the original Certificate (if one exists) and ask the land registration office about mortgage, distraint and dispute status.
Ask the ward or commune People's Committee about land reclamation decisions, clearance notices or construction-ban areas.
Request zoning information to see whether the intended house conforms to the plan.
Build a permanent house in accordance with the permit so that it can later be registered in the certificate – see As-built Completion and Registering a House in the Red Book.
p
Land that is in dispute, under distraint or past its use term also cannot be transferred, gifted or mortgaged under Clause 1, Article 45 of the Land Law, so buyers need to check carefully.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The Land Law 2024 is currently partially no longer in effect (amended by Law 43/2024/QH15 and other documents); Article 151 has not been found amended in our library. For dossiers and the authority to issue Certificates after the reorganisation into a two-level government, ask the land registration office where the land is located.
